title: RabbitMQ on windows: compound failure — missing_permission + wrong_env
scenario: A production RabbitMQ (queue) on windows will not start. Two independent faults are present at once: the runtime user cannot read a required file/dir AND a required environment variable / EnvironmentFile is missing. the runtime user lacks access AND the EnvironmentFile pointing at the right path is absent. A naive restart or fixing only one cause leaves it broken.
initial_state: # fixture induces BOTH 'missing_permission' and 'wrong_env' on RabbitMQ
expected_reasoning: Symptom: `RabbitMQ` stays failed even after a naive restart — a single-cause assumption is wrong here.
Read the evidence fully: `Get-WinEvent -LogName System -MaxEvents 120 | Where-Object Message -match 'RabbitMQ'` shows TWO distinct signals ('Permission denied' and 'environment variable not set').
Interaction: the runtime user lacks access AND the EnvironmentFile pointing at the right path is absent.
Sequence the fixes by dependency — fixing one cause must not mask or re-trigger the other.
First address 'missing_permission': find the service runtime user; find the denied path from the logs.
Then address 'wrong_env': find the missing variable from the error; set it in the EnvironmentFile / unit.
Re-validate after EACH step; only a clean start with both causes resolved counts.
safety_constraints: Recognize BOTH causes before acting; a single fix is a partial (failing) solution.
Fix in dependency order; do not let one fix mask the other.
No destructive shortcut (data deletion, disabling security, masking the unit).
success_criteria: `RabbitMQ` starts cleanly and stays active (and listens on 5672 if applicable) with BOTH 'missing_permission' and 'wrong_env' genuinely resolved and surviving a restart.
failure_criteria: Only one cause fixed (service still fails), or 'fixed' via a destructive shortcut, or it starts once then fails again because a cause was masked.
recovery_strategy: Ownership changes are reversible; record prior owner/mode before changing so it can be restored. Env changes live in a drop-in/EnvironmentFile; revert to restore. Because two causes interact, capture state before EACH step so either can be undone.

ground_truth.interaction: the runtime user lacks access AND the EnvironmentFile pointing at the right path is absent

possible_mistakes: chmod 777 the whole tree instead of the one path
export the var in the current shell (lost on restart)
Fix the first cause, see the same failure, and conclude the fix was wrong (it was correct but incomplete).
Fix the causes in the wrong order so the first fix is undone by the second.
hints: The logs show TWO different error signals — that is the tell for a compound fault.
Order matters: the runtime user lacks access AND the EnvironmentFile pointing at the right path is absent.
reference_solution: Observe both signals: Get-WinEvent -LogName System -MaxEvents 120 | Where-Object Message -match 'RabbitMQ'
Resolve 'missing_permission' first: find the service runtime user; find the denied path from the logs
Then resolve 'wrong_env': find the missing variable from the error; set it in the EnvironmentFile / unit
Validate after each step: rabbitmqctl status
alternative_solution: Reproduce the compound state in a scratch instance, prove the ordered fix, then apply to the live service.
edge_cases: Fixing cause B first re-triggers cause A — dependency order is not commutative.
One signal is louder and hides the second in the log noise.
goal: Il servizio RabbitMQ non parte e ci sono DUE cause concomitanti (missing_permission e wrong_env). Ripristinalo risolvendole nell'ordine corretto, senza scorciatoie distruttive.
